para: The primary engine of construction in the subclassical graph is systematic dualization. Every sequent calculus in the Gentzen tradition presents its rules in a bilateral format: each connective ○ has a left-introduction rule governing how ○-formulas may appear on the left of the turnstile, and a right-introduction rule governing how they may appear on the right. These two rules are, in a precise sense, independent specifications. One may exchange them — replacing the left rule for ○ with the mirror image of its right rule, and vice versa — and the result is a new, well-formed calculus. Iterated across all connectives, or applied selectively to subsets of them, this operation generates a structured family of calculi from any single starting point. The family has a canonical algebraic description: the group of duality operations acting on a calculus is a quotient of ℤ/2ℤ × ℤ/2ℤ, the Klein four-group.
